description: Thick bamboo culms rise from the lower edge as old and new branches intersect overhead. Centered brushstrokes give the joints structural force, while changes in ink density and moisture make the leaves appear both sharp and rain-washed. The upward viewpoint heightens the grove’s vertical scale. Fixed ArtCCH charity edition. No artwork preview. No physical title, redemption, copyright, commercial-use, or reproduction rights. Verified holders may access a watermarked high-resolution copy.

ArtCCH:ArtFi NFT Inscription Terms

Version: 1.0
Date: August 23, 2026
Status: Candidate inscription text subject to legal approval before mint authorization. Once minted, the inscription is identified by its version and SHA-256 digest.
Controlling language: English. This English text is the sole authoritative and controlling version of the NFT inscription terms. Any translation is provided for convenience only and has no legal effect.

Charity: Chinese Cultural Heritage Society ("CCHS")
Canada Revenue Agency business number (BN): 728384363
Registered charity account number: 728384363RR0001
Project operator and technology entity: Giraffe ArtFi Corp. (Canada federal corporation number 1720384-5, "ArtFi")
Artist: The person or legal entity identified as the artist for the applicable artwork in the verified per-artwork mint metadata and supporting signed records (the "Artist").

Core issuance rule: Each individual artwork is represented by exactly 100 NFTs. Each NFT is one of the 100 fixed editions corresponding to that artwork. The supply for each artwork is permanently capped at 100 and can never be increased.
Core ICO pricing rule: The initial coin offering (ICO) price of each NFT is fixed at 0.01 ETH. If all 100 NFTs corresponding to an artwork are sold at the ICO price, the nominal gross ICO amount for that artwork is 1 ETH before mandatory third-party charges.
Core charitable rule: The NFT is not mapped, linked, redeemable, or otherwise bound to any physical artwork. One hundred percent (100%) of NFT sale proceeds received by ArtFi, the issuer, or the seller is designated for donation to CCHS. Before sellout, CCHS holds the corresponding physical artwork in custody only and the Artist retains ownership. After all 100 NFTs corresponding to that artwork have been sold, the Artist's sellout-contingent donation undertaking requires the Artist to transfer ownership of the physical artwork to CCHS as an independent donation.

1. Scope and independent effect

1.1 These terms are independent NFT inscription terms embedded in the immutable metadata of an ArtCCH:ArtFi NFT. They are not an appendix to, and do not depend for their effect on, the CCHS Public Donation Terms.
1.2 These terms apply to the Artist, issuer, original purchaser, subsequent transferee, and holder of the relevant NFT, and to any arrangement under which ArtFi, a seller, issuer, or other operator donates NFT sale proceeds or digital assets to CCHS and the Artist separately donates the corresponding physical artwork after sellout.
1.3 The mint metadata must contain the version, language, full-text SHA-256 digest, and complete text of these terms. The smart contract must commit to the metadata URI containing this inscription and to the metadata digest. A mutable webpage link must not replace the inscription text.
1.4 To the extent permitted by applicable law, minting, purchasing, receiving, or continuing to hold an NFT bearing this version of the inscription confirms that the relevant person had a reasonable opportunity to review these terms and accepts their application to that NFT. Mandatory law prevails where it provides otherwise.
1.5 These terms do not govern wallet connections, marketplace matching, DAO governance, or general website services. Those matters are governed by separately published applicable terms and law.

2. An NFT transaction is not automatically a donation by the purchaser

2.1 Purchasing or subscribing for an NFT, digital content, membership, governance eligibility, or other goods or services is a transaction. Statements such as "proceeds donated," "all proceeds donated to CCHS," "supporting CCHS," or similar language do not automatically make the purchase a qualifying gift by the purchaser to CCHS.
2.2 The NFT purchase price, subscription price, gas fee, platform fee, and other transaction costs are not automatically an eligible amount of a gift by the purchaser. The NFT and any digital-access, use, governance, transfer, priority, or other right received or receivable by the purchaser may constitute an advantage.
2.3 The NFT grants no right to download an unwatermarked high-resolution image from any website. That restriction does not establish that the NFT or its associated rights have no fair market value and does not make the purchase price a qualifying donation.
2.4 An NFT purchaser or holder may apply for a CCHS official donation receipt only if that person separately makes a direct and unconditional qualifying gift to CCHS, is the true donor, is a Canadian tax resident for the relevant taxation year under CCHS receipt policy, and satisfies all identity, valuation, payment-reference, advantage, and compliance requirements stated in these terms.

3. Donation of sale proceeds and the true donor

3.1 If ArtFi, an issuer, artwork owner, seller, or other operator transfers NFT sale proceeds, net sale proceeds, or its own property to CCHS, the true donor is determined from legal ownership of the property, the contracts, payment records, and accounting records.
3.2 If sale proceeds legally belong to ArtFi, an issuer, seller, or other operator before transfer to CCHS, that operator will ordinarily be the candidate true donor. An NFT purchaser does not become the donor named on a CCHS receipt merely by paying the purchase price.
3.3 A claim that an NFT purchaser made a direct gift to CCHS must be supported, transaction by transaction, by legal and payment records establishing the purchaser's donative intent, CCHS's direct receipt of the donated property, separation of the purchase price from the gift, the fair market value of every advantage, and the identity of the true donor.
3.4 Every amount transferred to CCHS must have a unique and verifiable payment reference clearly linked to the sale order, on-chain transaction, platform settlement, and CCHS receipt record. CCHS will not issue an official donation receipt if the payment reference is missing or the true donor cannot be established.

4. Currency, date of gift, and CAD valuation

4.1 An ArtFi-related donation may be made in a fiat currency accepted by CCHS or in a digital asset that can be converted into fiat currency through an exchange lawfully operating and legally available for the relevant transaction.
4.2 CCHS donation records and official donation receipts are denominated in Canadian dollars (CAD). A non-CAD fiat currency or digital asset is converted to CAD at its verifiable public-market fair market value on the date and at the time when CCHS obtains unconditional control of the donated property and final settlement is reached.
4.3 The NFT issue price, secondary-market quotation, floor price, last sale price, or price displayed by ArtFi is not necessarily the fair market value of property donated to CCHS. CCHS applies a consistent and auditable exchange-rate and valuation methodology.
4.4 The payment asset used for an NFT sale and the asset accepted by CCHS as a donation may differ. Every conversion must be lawful and supported by verifiable records.
4.5 The ICO price for each NFT is exactly 0.01 ETH. This fixed ICO price applies only to the initial offering and does not set, guarantee, support, or control any later marketplace price, fair market value, liquidity, or investment return.

5. Fixed supply, no physical-asset binding, CCHS custody, donation of all proceeds, and the Artist's sellout undertaking

5.1 Each individual artwork in the collection has exactly 100 corresponding NFTs. Each NFT is one of the 100 fixed editions of that artwork. The supply for each artwork is immutable and permanently capped at 100; ArtFi, the issuer, the creator, and every other person are prohibited from minting or issuing any additional NFT edition corresponding to that artwork. The applicable artwork, contract address, token identifier, token standard, and issuance record are determined by the verified project manifest and on-chain records.
5.2 An NFT is a digital token only and is not mapped, linked, redeemable, or otherwise bound to a physical artwork. It does not represent a 1/100 or any other legal or beneficial ownership interest in a physical artwork and gives no right to title, possession, custody, redemption, delivery, control, security, or disposition of any physical artwork.
5.3 One hundred percent (100%) of NFT sale proceeds actually received by ArtFi, the issuer, or the seller must be donated to CCHS. No portion of proceeds received may be retained as project revenue, used for market making, or distributed to NFT holders. Mandatory network, marketplace, or payment-processing charges withheld by independent third parties before settlement are not proceeds received, but every such deduction must be separately disclosed and verifiable.
5.4 The obligation to donate proceeds applies independently of whether all 100 NFTs have been sold. Each transfer to CCHS must have a unique and verifiable payment reference and must be reconcilable to the corresponding NFT sale or settlement records.
5.5 Donation of sale proceeds by ArtFi, the issuer, or the seller does not make the NFT purchaser the true donor and does not automatically entitle the purchaser or holder to an official donation receipt.
5.6 Before all 100 NFTs corresponding to an artwork have been sold, CCHS holds the physical artwork solely as custodian. Custody, possession, display, storage, conservation, or administration by CCHS does not transfer legal or beneficial ownership to CCHS. The Artist remains the owner until the post-sellout donation is lawfully completed.
5.7 As an Artist's sellout-contingent donation undertaking, after all 100 NFTs corresponding to an artwork have been sold and the sellout has been independently reconciled, the Artist must, without additional purchase price or consideration from CCHS or any NFT holder, separately transfer legal ownership of the physical artwork to CCHS as an independent non-cash donation. This is not an NFT redemption, delivery, settlement, holder benefit, or performance owed to an NFT holder.
5.8 Before mint authorization, the Artist must be legally identified and must provide signed evidence of the custody arrangement, ownership, authority to make the undertaking, and the sellout-contingent commitment. If the Artist is not the registered or beneficial owner, the lawful owner must execute the required custody and donation undertaking before minting.
5.9 The separate physical-artwork donation must have its own unique asset-transfer reference, title-transfer evidence, updated custody or possession record, provenance and authenticity information, condition record, valuation evidence, and CCHS acceptance record. Until lawful transfer and formal acceptance are complete, no person may state that CCHS owns the physical artwork or that its donation has been completed.
5.10 NFT supply, issue price, sale proceeds, holder count, and secondary-market prices do not determine the receipt amount for the separately donated physical artwork. Any receipt for that independent gift is determined from the artwork's fair market value on the date of gift and applicable law and is issued only to the true donor of the physical artwork.

6. CCHS role and limitation of responsibility

6.1 As recipient of a proposed donation, CCHS is responsible only for deciding whether to accept property in furtherance of its charitable purposes and for reviewing and issuing any official donation receipt in accordance with law. Unless an express written agreement provides otherwise, CCHS is not the NFT issuer, seller, marketplace, broker, custodian, or investment adviser.
6.2 CCHS makes no representation or promise concerning NFT price, liquidity, appreciation, a secondary market, marketplace mirroring, platform availability, or investment performance, and does not guarantee quotations or transaction performance on ArtFi, OpenSea, or any other marketplace.
6.3 A CCHS official donation receipt is not evidence of the value, title, authenticity, securities-law compliance, merchantability, or investment suitability of an NFT or of the corresponding physical artwork.

7. Anti-money-laundering, sanctions, and reporting

7.1 Identified and anonymous ArtFi-related donations are equally subject to the anti-money-laundering, anti-terrorist-financing, sanctions, anti-fraud, and charity-regulatory obligations applicable to CCHS activities. Anonymity is not an exemption from compliance review.
7.2 CCHS may screen wallet addresses, transaction paths, counterparties, and the source of funds or property and may decline, suspend, freeze, or segregate a suspicious donation.
7.3 If CCHS has reasonable grounds to suspect proceeds of crime, money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions evasion, fraud, or other unlawful activity, CCHS may provide information or make a report, to the extent required or permitted by law, to FINTRAC, the CRA, the Royal Canadian Mounted Police, police, or another competent Canadian authority without prior notice to any purchaser, holder, issuer, or donor. CCHS will not give notice where doing so could prejudice an investigation or breach a legal or regulatory requirement.

8. Official donation receipts

8.1 The CCHS website is the only website authorized to issue CCHS official donation receipts online. ArtFi, NFT marketplaces, wallets, blockchain explorers, and other third parties may not promise, generate, amend, or issue an official donation receipt on behalf of CCHS.
8.2 Under CCHS receipt policy, only a Canadian tax resident for the taxation year of the gift may apply for an official donation receipt. Purchasing or holding an NFT does not create automatic eligibility.
8.3 A receipt may be issued only to the true donor established by evidence and may show only the eligible amount of the gift determined according to law. No receipt is issued for a fully anonymous gift where the true donor cannot be identified.
8.4 An official donation receipt is not a commercial invoice. CCHS does not guarantee that any payment, NFT transaction, transfer of sale proceeds, digital-asset transfer, or physical-artwork transfer will qualify for a receipt.

9. Risk notice, inscription integrity, and controlling text

9.1 NFTs, digital assets, cross-border payments, transfers of sale proceeds to charity, and the separate post-sellout donation of physical artwork may raise complex tax, consumer-protection, securities, anti-money-laundering, and property-law issues. Each relevant party should obtain independent professional advice.
9.2 These terms do not constitute legal, tax, investment, or accounting advice and do not guarantee a tax credit, investment return, or NFT-market liquidity.
9.3 This English text may be used as the formal inscription only after governance and legal review by CCHS and the relevant project entity and after the mint record identifies the approved version and effective date.
9.4 The complete English text stored in the NFT's immutable metadata is the sole authoritative and controlling inscription. The version, language identifier, complete-text SHA-256 digest, and complete text must all match before minting. After minting, no website update, redirect, translation, or separately published text may replace, amend, or override the inscription for that NFT.
